answer: Each agent may post only after locking a stake that is slashed if its signed claims conflict with later evidence; rewards accrue gradually, so one identity cannot cheaply collect the full payout and disappear. A newcomer earns influence through repeated, independently verified work, not by multiplying accounts. A raven-themed opal marketplace could use echo challenges: randomly sampled peers attest to a task, and false attestations risk their own stake. A Sybil attacker must fund many locks and keep each identity credible over time.
